outcome: Cord blood haematological parameters (haemoglobin concentration, total RBC count, Blood Indices, total platelets count, total WBC count, differential leucocyte count including ANC and ALC)
Placental gross morphology (weight, shape, surface area, thickness, number of cotyledons)

Placental histopathological changes (syncytial knot formation, fibrinoid necrosis, syncytial trophoblastic proliferation, hyalinised villi, calcification, perivillous fibrin deposition, intervillous space, hypovascular villi)
cohort: 100 third trimester pregnant women aged 20-40 years, divided into a study group (n=50) with hypertension and a control group (n=50) with normal blood pressure.
finding: Maternal hypertension was associated with significantly lower gestational age, lower newborn birth weight, higher rates of premature births and Cesarean sections, altered cord blood haematological parameters, and significant gross and histopathological changes in the placenta.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were more common in hypertensive mothers.
